speakers.name: Yu Cheng
speakers.bio: Yu Cheng is a Ph.D student in School of Computer Science at Peking University, he is a core developer of TileLang, a programming language for AI workload on various hardware platforms.

speakers.name: Megan Knight
speakers.bio: Megan Knight is the Director of Software Communities at Arm where she leads engineering initiatives and upstream engagements with open source communities. She holds many leadership positions across the software stack including Governing Board Member and Global Cyber Policy Workgroup Lead for OpenSSF, Board Member and Advocacy Chair for the Yocto Project, Steering Committee and OSPO SIG Lead for UXL Foundation, and Governing Board Member for Zephyr Project. Prior to Arm, Megan was building the IoT and Automotive open source portfolio at Amazon Web Services and launching projects in neutral spaces including Valkey.

speakers.name: Cailean Osborne
speakers.bio: Cailean is Head of Ecosystem Development at Probabl, the company founded by the creators of scikit-learn.

speakers.name: Merel Theisen
speakers.bio: I am a Principal Software Engineer at QuantumBlack, where I am currently the tech lead of Kedro, an open-source project part of the Linux Foundation. I have over ten years of experience in the software industry, with most of my career focused on backend product engineering. I am passionate about building products that solve real user problems, and I care deeply about creating robust, well-tested software that follows good engineering principles. I am also a strong advocate for open-source software, and I find working with the community to be both inspiring and energising.

speakers.name: Chi Wang
speakers.bio: Creator of AutoGen (AG2). Senior Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind. Research focus: agentic AI systems, multi-agent coordination, and autonomous agents. Built Sutando, a personal AI agent with real-time voice, vision, and autonomous action. Building MassGen for scalable parallel agent execution.
speakers.roleOrg: Senior Staff Research Scientist, Google DeepMind

speakers.name: Wei Wang
speakers.bio: Wei Wang is the Director of the Open Source Technology Committee at Singularity Intelligence Research Institute, Head of the Open Source Governance Standards Working Group at the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's Electronics Standards Institute, Secretary-General of the UN Consultative Open Source Innovation Committee, and Professor at East China Normal University. He is a Distinguished Member of CCF. He led the development of China's first set of open source governance standards, with research focusing on open source governance and evaluation. He has published over 100 papers in top conferences and journals including ICSE, WWW, and ACL.

speakers.name: Jiaju Zhang
speakers.bio:
Jiaju Zhang is a passionate open-source advocate with over 20 years of experience in R&D, architectural design, and engineering management. His expertise spans Linux, distributed systems, cloud-native technologies, and AI infrastructure. Throughout his career, Jiaju has held senior leadership roles, including Chief Architect, Technical Director and Head of R&D in China, at major multinational and ICT enterprises. As an independent contributor, he has successfully launched and promoted globally recognized open-source projects.

Currently, Jiaju serves as Chief Architect in Field CTO Organization, Red Hat, focuses on advancing open source AI communities like vLLM and llm-d and fostering enterprise solutions through co-engineering with ecosystem partners. His work is instrumental in driving AI technology strategy and accelerating the industrial deployment of Red Hat solutions across various vertical sectors.
